transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this design review meeting. As you know, we're here to go over the draft proposal for the outdoor learning garden at Oak Ridge Elementary serving grades 3 through 5. Before I make any final decisions on the design, safety plan, or funding, I'd like to hear from each of you. Let's start with the facilities manager -- could you walk us through your review of the proposal, particularly regarding the West Courtyard location and the six soil beds, open compost tumbler, flowering plants, and student water station?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Vega. I need to raise an urgent issue before we go any further. A facilities soil test completed this week found contamination in the West Courtyard. I received the lab report after the draft proposal was circulated, so the site plan hasn't been updated yet. Under district grounds policy, this means the garden cannot be placed in the West Courtyard. We need to relocate it to the East Courtyard and use sealed raised beds there instead of the standard soil beds currently in the proposal. This will also likely affect the materials cost estimate.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Brooks. That's an important catch on the West Courtyard contamination. I do have an update from my end as well. The grade 3 through 5 lesson sequence was finalized just this week, after the draft proposal was written, and it actually requires exactly four raised beds rather than the six soil beds currently listed in the proposal. It also calls for two lidded compost bins instead of the one open compost tumbler. So if we're relocating to the East Courtyard with sealed raised beds as you've suggested, we'd want to make sure we're planning for the correct number of beds and compost bins based on the lesson rotations. I'll need to get those equipment changes formally entered into the proposal before Dr. Vega makes a final decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Before we finalize the safety plan, I need to flag a health concern that hasn't been entered into the draft proposal yet. Two participating students have documented severe contact reactions to latex and soil-borne irritants. I confirmed against their health records this week that our student health plan requires nitrile gloves for all student use in the garden, and a handwashing station must be located within 10 feet of the soil beds. These requirements need to be added to the proposal before Dr. Vega approves the final design and safety plan.

transcript.text: Thank you, everyone. I need to share an important funding update before we finalize anything. I reviewed the executed garden grant award this week, and it covers exactly $3,200 of eligible materials. However, the grant agreement requires all garden materials to be purchased through a grant purchase order rather than the general fund. The draft proposal currently lists the general fund as the funding source, so that needs to be corrected. I have not yet attached the award documentation to the proposal, but I'll make sure it's included once we've incorporated all the design and safety changes we've discussed today.
